Kinds now match (A helpful, I; B sunny, us), but only adjective and pronoun are asked. Noun, verb and adverb never are, and the lesson's main misconception, every -ly word read as an adverb, goes untested. Add a third card per form: A softly, B neatly (adverbs in the bank).

Fixed. Each form has one comma joining word and one 'because' with no comma (', or' + because; ', and' + because). The new direction quotes the four joining words. One answer each.
Fixed. Three cards per form, one simple (with list commas, in both), one complex and one compound. Keys right. Minor: same order of kinds in both forms.
Fixed. Each form asks for the plain form, a superlative and a comparative, mixing -er/-est with more/most (A colorful, fastest, more patiently; B helpful, most exciting, bigger). One answer each.

Unchanged and right.

instruction.K-667: I will read the sentence. Put a dot where you start reading. Draw arrows to show the way you read: across the line, then back to the start of the next line.

worksheet: G2-546 (Long Vowels in Two-Syllable Words, vowels-g2b.en.json syll.sentences level 1): all 13 rewrites are true, natural US English, one answer each. One echo is left: 'Put on your ___. It is raining.' → raincoat (rain/raining). Rewrite: 'Put on your ___ so you stay dry.'

G3-516 (Base Words and Suffixes, new -ness/-ment sentence cards): three do not sound like US English. 'Running every day is good for your fitness' → 'Our gym teacher checks our fitness.' 'Smell the freshness of the bread' → 'I love the freshness of warm bread.' 'The wetness of the grass soaked my socks' → 'I could feel the wetness of the grass through my socks.' The rest are fine. -able (in the lesson title) has no sentence card.

G2-548 / G3-518 hearts: unstressed vowels are treated unevenly. 'because' hearts its e and its se (/z/), and 'ocean' hearts ea, but 'does' leaves s = /z/ unhearted and 'again', 'enough', 'island' and 'special' leave their unstressed vowel unhearted. The key says a heart on a hearted part is right but not whether an extra heart costs the point. Add: 'An extra heart on a vowel that says /uh/, or on s that says /z/, does not lose the point.'
G2-548 key note: '(because is not asked: three of its parts can be called tricky)' tells a teacher about a word that is not on the page. Drop it.

G3-533 (Which Plural Is Right?) and G3-526 (Possessive Nouns): still open from the first review. Neither bank has a truly irregular plural (mice, teeth, feet, children) or an irregular plural possessive (the children's coats), though both lesson objectives name them.

Picture withdrawal: the code withdraws ship, beach and the lamb-like sheep only in G1-380/K-378 (types/g1/G1-380-digraphs.js WITHDRAWN). G1-586 (Long e: ee and ea) still prints summer/beach and animals/sheep on English pages, so 'withdrawn wherever they stood in English' is not accurate. With the b__ch and sh__p frames both pictures are fair; the beach is only a poor, tiny scene.

G1-380 English check bank (CHECK_EN): th has only thumb (start) and tooth (end), so the two forms can never ask th in the same place. Add one more th picture: three or thumbtack at the start, or moth or bath at the end.
notes: Key colors: the answer rings are now orange everywhere, but written answers on lines are still teal in several keys (G1-305 scoops, the G2/G3 fill-in lines). On a gray-scale copy they show; consistency only.

Earlier findings (see earlierFindings): 39 fixed, 2 partly (k-words 'cubes'; G1-586 beach and sheep), 3 open and minor (word-count order; no true irregular plural in G3-533 or plural possessive in G3-526), 1 overtaken. New: g3-reading part 2 lost consonant-le; g3-parts-of-speech part 1 should ask an adverb.
